properties.name: Reviewed: gap:a3a499e09447e1e3
properties.rationale:
ACCEPTED WHILE PLANNED, AND NOW DATED — Anthony's call 2026-07-31, taken with the other three of its kind as one judgement.

The gap's literal question — "how will you confirm it?" — is ALREADY ANSWERED: ver:tool-carries-convention is written and sits at `planned`, pinning that the convention rides the tool AND stays bounded (checked against a named list, so adding a tool without considering it is caught, and no description exceeds its budget). What the gap reports is that the check has never RUN, which is true of anything unbuilt.

WHY ACCEPT RATHER THAN LEAVE OPEN: these four were the only notes on the gate, so every cut printed "5 notes" with no way to tell signal from permanent background — which is how a gate stops being read. When the capability is built and its check passes, the gap disappears on its own.

*** CORRECTION, MADE THE SAME DAY, LEFT ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN EDITED AWAY. *** This rationale originally claimed `cap:review-expires-on-content` would bring the gap back if the capability were reworded. THAT IS FALSE — that capability is PLANNED, NOT BUILT. Expiry keys on the gap id, which hashes affected node IDS, so a review expires when the affected SET changes membership and NEVER on CONTENT change. This review does NOT self-expire; reword the capability and someone must revisit it BY HAND. Demonstrated live the same hour on the sibling acknowledgement decision:ack:4f9dcb95353889c2, where a substantial rewrite left the old judgement suppressing the gap against new text.

WHY IT IS SCHEDULED AND NOT MERELY ACCEPTED: all four were scheduled against NOTHING, so quieting them would have relied on someone remembering. Now SCHEDULED_FOR rel:v0210 as `expected`, so arrival_delta asks at v0.21.0 regardless.

WORTH CARRYING TO THE BUILD: this one is bounded at a sentence per tool ON PURPOSE, because descriptions are context paid for on EVERY session and cap:tool-search exists precisely because the surface is already large. It does not reverse dec:skills-served — the served skill keeps the depth and the worked examples; the tool carries only the irreducible minimum an agent would reconstruct wrongly or not at all.

DELIBERATELY NOT IN v0.20.0, which Anthony scoped to cap:changelog-view alone.
